== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Migrating Ancestor|origin= Ireland |destination= New Zealand|origin-flag= Flags-1.gif |destination-flag= Flags-19.png}}
{{New Zealand Sticker | region=Auckland | place=Papakura}}
Diamond Wedding; Mr & Mrs Glasgow - Mr & Mrs J Glasgow of Papakura, celebrated their diamond wedding on Saturday. A large number of their family & friends gather at their residence in honour of the event.
Mr Glasgow is the youngest son of the late Mr & Mrs William Glasgow, of Montolier, Ireland, & he was married on June 29, 1875, at the Presbyterian Church at Orritor, County Tyrone, Ireland. Mrs Glasgow was formerly Miss Margaret Dougall, third daughter of the late Mr and Mrs T Dougall, of Killycurragh. About a week after their wedding Mr & Mrs Glasgow left for New Zealand on the sailing ship 'British Empire'.
On arrival at Auckland Mr & Mrs Glasgow first took up their residence at Epsom. Mr Glasgow worked principally for the late Mr Dilworth, being in charge of stock on his farm at Onehunga. The old punt service had then only recently been abandoned and a wooden bridge erected, giving access to Mangere. Mr Glasgow took up a farm just across the bridge. From there he commenced a dairy supply, serving the Onehunga district. This was carried on by his family for over 40years. Mr Glasgow served for a number of years as a member of the Mangere Road Board & the Mangere School committee. His principal interest, however, was in the Presbyterian Church at Onehunga.
Fifteen years ago Mr & Mrs Glasgow moved to Papakura. of a family of 11 Children, 10 are living.
Numerous messages of congratulations have reach Mr & Mrs Glasgow during the week-end
A marriage for James Glasgow and Dougal was registered on 29 June 1875 in the Cookstown district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 29 June 1875, Cookstown district, M/1875/L1/1132/1/196.</ref>

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-585]] is assessed at 98% (proved). James’s held 1935 diamond-wedding notice explicitly calls him youngest son of the late Mr and Mrs William Glasgow of Montolier/Montober. His 1875 Orritor marriage, spouse and migration narrative distinguish the specific family; the father’s held account also cites James’s certificate naming Mary Henry.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.
